spec_match.rationale: The two comma rules (size OR style() branch) are valid, well-chosen spec usage, but the page's firing readouts re-implement the conditions in JS arithmetic instead of observing the cascade, so what it reports is not the spec behaviour.

interactive.rationale: Two real toggle buttons set the custom properties, the container is drag-resizable with a ResizeObserver width readout, and the rule panel updates live (assessed from code review and the rendered DOM; the controls were not driven in this session).

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises a product card switching on width OR a custom-property flag with toggles — matching the page.

edge_cases.rationale: No capability detection: in this pre-150 browser both comma rules are parser-dropped, the toggles visibly do nothing, and the readouts still claim 'rule 1 firing: yes / rule 2 firing: yes' over a stacked short-description card (screenshot evidence).

references.rationale: Fixed 2026-10-04 (weekly hardening): the page now links https://chromestatus.com/feature/6196591858941952, matching its feature index — restoring invariant 3 and the fix-slugs self-heal. Verified by grep against the canonical id on the feature index.

conformance.rationale: The shared feature suite proves real parse/CSSOM contracts and honestly fails 4 of 5 here.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Cloud-fallback observation only, NOT browser-verified per auto-research.md §0 — headless Chromium 141 (full-page screenshot + DOM, not chrome-devtools-mcp): at 712px the readouts claim both rules fire while the card renders stacked with the short description — toggles and drag-resize were not driven. chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud session (the auto-research.md section-0 blocker applies, so this is NOT browser verification): what was exercised is page load, full-page screenshot read, served/dumped DOM state and the /conformance/ route result; driving every control and capturing console/network evidence remains for an MCP-equipped session.

telemetry_health.rationale: Baseline injected telemetry only; no interaction/assert events that would have exposed the readout-vs-render mismatch.

design_system.rationale: Variables throughout; card-btn.primary and toggle-btn.active set background and color together.

accessibility.rationale: Toggles are native buttons but lack aria-pressed, the rule indicators are colour-only dots paired with text that is not live-announced, and the decorative Add-to-cart/Wishlist buttons are focusable no-ops.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Readouts and toggles wrap and the card is fluid; clean at 1280px headless, but drag-resize is the only way to drive the width branch on touch (toggles only cover the style() branch) and the ≈360px class was not exercised.

openQuestions.title: Read rule state from the rendered card, not from JS re-implementation
openQuestions.detail: updateReadout() computes `forceWide || w > 360` and reports it as 'rule firing'. In this Chromium 141 session the panel said both rules fire while the card was visibly stacked with the short description, because the comma rules never parsed. Observe getComputedStyle(.card-inner).flexDirection and .card-desc-full display instead, label which branch produced the match, and show an explicit 'comma-separated @container unsupported — requires Chrome 150+' notice when the observed style disagrees with the expected condition.

openQuestions.title: Expose toggle state and announce rule changes
openQuestions.detail: Add aria-pressed to the two force-flag toggles and make the rules-active panel (or the readout row) a polite live region so flag flips and rule transitions are perceivable non-visually; consider also disabling or inerting the decorative Add-to-cart/Wishlist buttons so they are not focusable dead ends.

openQuestions.title: Offer a non-drag way to drive the width branch
openQuestions.detail: The style() branch has buttons but the width branch only has the CSS resize corner, which keyboard and most touch users cannot operate. Add width preset buttons or a slider wired to the container so both OR branches are drivable on every device.

summary: Reviewed with the headless-Chromium-141 cloud fallback (not chrome-devtools-mcp): full-page screenshot + DOM of /v149/comma-separated-container-queries/or-condition-component/ and the feature /conformance/ route (HTTP 200; panel 1 pass / 4 fail / 0 blocked). The concept — one rule, two trigger axes, with toggles for the style() branch — is strong, but the firing readouts are JS arithmetic that contradicted the rendered card in this browser (claimed yes/yes over a stacked, short-description card), the page lacks its ChromeStatus anchor, and there is no unsupported notice. Button toggles and drag-resize were not driven headless.
